messages:
oncall-bot: [ALERT] severity=sev2 service=continuous-batching path=streaming p95=350ms p99=2200ms incident=INC-199876
marta (oncall): Paging — we're seeing a tail spike on the continuous-batching path, streaming stalls reported by internal QA. p99 ~2.2s, p95 ~350ms. Investigating now.
lee (eng-runtime): Ack. Looking at scheduler and batching graphs. Any recent deploys or config changes in the last 6 hours?
jin (sre): No deploys besides the 02:10 UTC rolling worker restart. SRE: queue_depth for cont-batch streaming spiked to ~1200 at 01:55 UTC, GPU utilization low (~40%).
samuel (infra): KV metrics: one Redis shard saw eviction spikes ~01:58 UTC but not total outages. Disk/network fine.
lee (eng-runtime): Reproduced locally with mixed-seqlen replay: long sequences (600-1200 tokens) get grouped into large batches and hold KV/cache and streaming tokens — small streaming requests get starved. Cont-batch policy is too aggressive.
lee (eng-runtime): Quick mitigation suggestion: disable continuous batching for streaming endpoints and cap batch tokens. I'll flip flags for prod streaming routes: `routing.continuous_batch.enabled=false` and `batch.max_tokens=512`.
marta (oncall): Go ahead. I'll start customer impact assessment and notify CS.
oncall-bot: change requested by lee at 1998765698 — awaiting apply.
lee (eng-runtime): Applying now via ops-runner:
```
ops-runner apply-config --service continuous-batching --env prod --set "routing.continuous_batch.enabled=false" --set "batch.max_tokens=512"
```
oncall-bot: change applied by lee at 1998765700 — rollout started.
jin (sre): Metric update: 2min after change p95 -> 140ms, p99 trending down to ~430ms. Queue depth reduced ~50%. Streaming stall counts dropped to near zero.
samuel (infra): Also set a temporary route-fallback for premium streaming customers to the smaller quantized model to avoid user-visible slowdowns: `route-policy set fallback=redwood/quant-small for tag:streaming-premium`
marta (oncall): Customer impact: CS tickets opened for three tenants (CS-9091/9092/9093) complaining about slow responses since ~01:50 UTC. No errors, just very high latency. Notifying account owners.
lee (eng-runtime): Root cause hypothesis: continuous-batching scheduler lacks preemptive fairness when mixing long and short sequences — a few oversized batches monopolize the batching tokens and KV, stalling streaming paths. Need scheduler changes: per-seqlen buckets + soft preemption after X ms + max_batch_tokens per route.
jin (sre): Agreed. Immediate post-incident actions: 1) keep cont-batch off for streaming 2) enforce `batch.max_tokens=512` globally for streaming routes 3) add alert: `contbatch.queue_depth > 800` and `contbatch.p99 > 700ms`
marta (oncall): I'll update the incident doc with timeline, mitigation steps, and customer comms. Current status: mitigated, monitoring. Leaving page open for handoff.
lee (eng-runtime): I'll start a canary for a fairness scheduler change in staging — design notes: token-based preemption and bucketed scheduling by seq-length; will push prototype tomorrow morning.
samuel (infra): Handoff in 20m. @samuel will take over next oncall. Tasks for handoff: gather trace dumps, capture KV eviction logs around 01:40-02:10 UTC, collect the batching scheduler profiles, and enumerate affected tenants.
samuel (infra): Taking handoff. I'll populate the postmortem with initial findings in ~45m and run a repro job against a mixed-seqlen workload to verify the fix surface.
marta (oncall): Thanks — leaving note: if p99 rises above 700ms re-escalate to sev1. Also add runbook item: default streaming config should have cont-batch disabled unless tenant explicitly opts in.
lee (eng-runtime): One rollback knob if needed: `service-scale --set-contbatch=0` to force traffic to stateless serving pool.
marta (oncall): Closing slack handoff; monitoring for 30m. If anything changes ping paging channel.
